editorial.description_en: Sunlight arriving through leaves — the colour of the light rather than of the leaf.
editorial.description_ja: 葉の間からもれる光のような、明るい黄緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.862, C 0.088, h 104.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 木 (ko, tree) + 漏れ (more, leaking) + 日 (bi, sunlight), after the standing word 木漏れ日. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Dappled Light" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 木漏日. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — haru-na at ΔE00 7.3, hina-gusa at ΔE00 8.1, mugi-batake at ΔE00 8.6. complementary is the entry nearest the opposite OKLCh hue (284°), within 22°. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
